key_insight: Flow-induced aggregation of TTAC/NaSal wormlike micelles can switch fluid friction from strong drag enhancement to drag reduction as flow conditions change.
engineering_relevance: Surfactant additives offer tunable friction control without the shear-induced degradation associated with high-molecular-weight polymer drag reducers.
method: Characterize TTAC/NaSal solutions using linear rheology and capillary pinch-off experiments.
Measure high-shear viscosity and laminar drag as flow-induced micellar structures develop.
Evaluate turbulent drag and vortex stability in Taylor–Couette flow across Reynolds numbers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 50% laminar drag enhancement, upwards of 200% turbulent drag enhancement, and up to 30% turbulent drag reduction at higher Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: Composition and operating conditions require careful selection because flow-induced aggregation can substantially increase drag before the drag-reducing regime is reached.
paper_title: Tuning fluid frictional drag through flow-induced aggregation of wormlike micelles
